title: Longitude Degree Distance Calculator
description: Convert a longitude-degree difference into east-west distance with the Longitude Degree Distance Calculator — at the span's own latitude. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the 0.2074 degrees of longitude between Times Square and JFK is 17.5 km of east-west ground at their latitude — and would be 23.1 km at the equator, which is why the latitude input exists.
quick_answer: The Longitude Degree Distance Calculator converts a longitude-degree difference into east-west distance at the latitude where the span actually lies. Enter the difference and the latitude and read kilometres or miles — the dedicated instrument for longitude spans, built around the cosine truth the general pages summarise.

A vendor's 'covers 500 km east-west' from a 5° span at 55°: 5 × 63.9 = 319 km. The calculator is the audit.
Degree-gridded data (climate cells, 1° tiles) has latitude-dependent ground size — this conversion is the cell-size table's engine.
2° of longitude: 222.6 km at the equator, 111.6 km at 60° — a factor of two from latitude alone. Any tool ignoring the input is selling the equator's answer to everyone.
From 179.5°E to 179.5°W is 1° of span — the short way across the seam. Differences should be taken the short way; the calculator assumes the true (smaller) difference you give it.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
East-west ground distance for a longitude-degree difference at a stated latitude, from WGS84 ellipsoid geometry.
Do I need an account?
No — difference and latitude in, distance out.
Can I rely on this for professional work?
For planning, reporting and verification, yes — ellipsoid-true numbers. Legal measurement remains survey practice.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — the frame GPS produces and web maps consume.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — resolution is not accuracy; the precision tools on this site price each decimal place in metres.
How does it differ from the Degrees Longitude page?
Same physics; this page is framed for a difference between two longitudes (a span), that one for degrees generally. Doorways differ, arithmetic agrees.
Very wide spans (90°)?
A quarter of the planet's girth at that latitude — the mid-latitude rate keeps it honest within a percent.
Southern latitudes?
Symmetric — −45° prices like +45°. The ellipsoid does not play hemispheric favourites.
Time zones again?
15° per solar hour at any latitude — but the kilometres per hour of longitude halve by 60°, computed above.
Polar research?
Near the pole longitude differences become metres — the calculator follows the geometry to its honest zero.
